ports.name: 2 Ship 2 Harkinian
ports.summary: Majora’s Mask, rebuilt from its decompiled source as a native Mac app, with enhancements and a randomizer.
ports.description: 2 Ship 2 Harkinian is a native port of Majora’s Mask built from the zeldaret decompilation on libultraship, from the team behind Ship of Harkinian. It extracts its assets from your ROM on first launch and adds frame interpolation, widescreen and a long list of optional changes to the camera, the three-day cycle, masks and saving. A randomizer and asset mods are built in.

ports.name: Starship
ports.summary: Star Fox 64, rebuilt from its decompiled source, with high frame rates and widescreen.
ports.description: Starship is a native port of Star Fox 64 built from the sonicdcer decompilation on libultraship. Frontport builds it from source and turns your ROM into its asset archive during the build. It renders with Metal, interpolates to your display’s frame rate, supports widescreen and loads asset packs from its mods folder.

ports.name: Zelda 64: Recompiled
ports.summary: Majora’s Mask, statically recompiled to native code, with high frame rates, widescreen and mod support.
ports.description: Zelda 64: Recompiled translates Majora’s Mask’s original N64 machine code into native code with N64Recomp and draws it with the RT64 renderer. It reads the game’s assets straight from your ROM, so there is no extraction step. It runs at any frame rate and in widescreen or ultrawide, and adds a dual-analog camera, gyro aiming and autosave. Code and texture mods load from its mods folder.

ports.name: Ghostship
ports.summary: Super Mario 64, rebuilt from its decompiled source, with a modern renderer and C mods compiled on the fly.
ports.description: Ghostship is a native port of Super Mario 64 built from the n64decomp decompilation on libultraship. It extracts its assets from your ROM, then renders with Metal at any frame rate and in widescreen. Its mod system compiles mods written in C while the game runs, and an online service signs mods and powers online mod features, so it needs the network. Extras include achievements, mirror mode and trackers.

ports.name: OpenGOAL
ports.summary: Jak and Daxter, decompiled and rebuilt as a native game.
ports.description: OpenGOAL decompiles Naughty Dog’s GOAL code for the Jak games back into readable source and compiles it with its own GOAL compiler into a native game. Frontport builds it from source, and its extractor turns your disc image into the playable game during the build. Jak and Daxter is complete, and the project has a live REPL and mod support.

ports.name: OpenGOAL
ports.summary: Jak II, decompiled and rebuilt as a native game.
ports.description: OpenGOAL decompiles Naughty Dog’s GOAL code for the Jak games back into readable source and compiles it with its own GOAL compiler into a native game. Frontport builds it from source, and its extractor turns your disc image into the playable game during the build. Upstream calls Jak II a beta: playable from start to finish, with a few known issues left to fix.

ports.name: OpenGOAL
ports.summary: Jak 3, decompiled and rebuilt as a native game.
ports.description: OpenGOAL decompiles Naughty Dog’s GOAL code for the Jak games back into readable source and compiles it with its own GOAL compiler into a native game. Frontport builds it from source, and its extractor turns your disc image into the playable game during the build. Upstream calls Jak 3 a beta: playable, with minor bugs and some instability left to fix.

ports.name: Banjo: Recompiled
ports.summary: Banjo-Kazooie, statically recompiled to native code, with high frame rates, widescreen and mod support.
ports.description: Banjo: Recompiled translates Banjo-Kazooie’s original N64 machine code into native code with N64Recomp, rendered by RT64. It reads the game’s assets straight from your ROM. It runs at high frame rates and in widescreen, and adds a dual-analog camera and optional note saving. Code and texture mods load from its mods folder.

ports.name: sm64coopdx
ports.summary: Online multiplayer Super Mario 64, built from its decompilation.
ports.description: sm64coopdx turns the Super Mario 64 PC port into an online co-op game in which every level, enemy and object stays in sync between players. You can host a game yourself or find one through its CoopNet lobbies. A large Lua modding API, model and level packs, and built-in mods such as Star Road and Hide and Seek come with it.

ports.name: Render96ex
ports.summary: Super Mario 64 with remade HD models and textures, built from its decompilation.
ports.description: Render96ex is the Super Mario 64 PC port with Render96’s remastered look: new high-polygon models for Mario and 100-odd characters and objects, an HD texture pack, and remixed music. Luigi and Wario are playable too, each with his own moves and voice. Frontport builds it from source with both packs and extracts the game’s original textures and sound from your ROM during the build. It runs at 60 FPS in any window shape and loads more model packs through DynOS.

ports.name: perfect_dark
ports.summary: Perfect Dark, built from its decompilation, with mouselook, widescreen and high frame rates.
ports.description: perfect_dark is the PC port of the Perfect Dark decompilation, with the single-player campaign, co-op and split-screen multiplayer working, though upstream still calls it a work in progress with minor graphics glitches. Frontport builds it from source and it reads levels, models and sound from your ROM. It adds mouselook and dual-analog controls, widescreen and a field-of-view setting, 60 FPS with fixes for frame-rate bugs, an experimental uncapped tick rate, custom levels as mods, and unlocks the Transfer Pak cheats without a Game Boy.

ports.name: zelda3
ports.summary: A Link to the Past, reimplemented in C from its reverse-engineered code.
ports.description: zelda3 is a reimplementation of A Link to the Past in tens of thousands of lines of C, reverse-engineered from the original SNES code and playable from start to finish. Frontport builds it from source and extracts its assets from your ROM during the build. It adds widescreen, shaders, higher-resolution Mode 7, MSU-1 audio, item switching and fixes for many of the original’s bugs.

ports.name: smw
ports.summary: Super Mario World, reimplemented in C from its reverse-engineered code.
ports.description: smw is a reimplementation of Super Mario World in C, reverse-engineered from the original SNES code by the author of zelda3 and playable from start to finish. Frontport builds it from source and extracts its levels and graphics from your ROM during the build. It removes the sprite limit per line, saves and replays snapshots, and draws through OpenGL shaders if you ask it to in smw.ini.

ports.name: sm
ports.summary: Super Metroid, reimplemented in C from its reverse-engineered code.
ports.description: sm is a reimplementation of Super Metroid in C, reverse-engineered from the original SNES code by the author of zelda3 and playable from start to finish, though upstream still calls it an early version with bugs. Frontport builds it from source and runs its own code only, reading levels and graphics from your ROM. It removes the sprite limit per line, draws the world map at a higher resolution, saves and replays snapshots, and draws through OpenGL shaders if you ask it to in sm.ini.

ports.name: UZDoom
ports.summary: Doom on the most capable Doom engine, in widescreen at any frame rate.
ports.description:
UZDoom carries on ZDoom and GZDoom, the Doom engine built up from the source code id Software released in 1997. It plays Doom with an OpenGL or Vulkan renderer at any frame rate, in widescreen and with mouselook, and its ZScript and ACS scripting run the largest library of mods any Doom engine has. Frontport installs it once per game, each with its own saves and settings, and Seeds your IWAD where UZDoom looks for it.

It takes Doom from 1.666 on, The Ultimate Doom, the BFG, Unity and 2024 releases, and the shareware episode. Frontport finds the ones Steam’s DOOM + DOOM II and DOOM 3: BFG Edition install in your Steam library.

ports.name: UZDoom
ports.summary: Doom II: Hell on Earth on the most capable Doom engine, in widescreen at any frame rate.
ports.description:
UZDoom carries on ZDoom and GZDoom, the Doom engine built up from the source code id Software released in 1997. It plays Doom II with an OpenGL or Vulkan renderer at any frame rate, in widescreen and with mouselook, and its ZScript and ACS scripting run the largest library of mods any Doom engine has. Frontport installs it once per game, each with its own saves and settings, and Seeds your IWAD where UZDoom looks for it.

It takes Doom II from 1.666 on and the BFG, Unity, Bethesda.net and 2024 releases. Frontport finds the ones Steam’s DOOM + DOOM II and DOOM 3: BFG Edition install in your Steam library.

ports.name: UZDoom
ports.summary: Heretic on the Doom engine it was built with, in widescreen at any frame rate.
ports.description:
UZDoom carries on ZDoom and GZDoom, the Doom engine built up from the source code id Software released in 1997. It plays Heretic with an OpenGL or Vulkan renderer at any frame rate, in widescreen and with mouselook, and its ZScript and ACS scripting run the largest library of mods any Doom engine has. Frontport installs it once per game, each with its own saves and settings, and Seeds your IWAD where UZDoom looks for it.

It takes Heretic 1.0, 1.2 and Shadow of the Serpent Riders, and the shareware episode. The 2025 re-release waits until UZDoom recognizes its IWAD.

ports.name: UZDoom
ports.summary: Hexen: Beyond Heretic, with its hubs and three classes, in widescreen at any frame rate.
ports.description:
UZDoom carries on ZDoom and GZDoom, the Doom engine built up from the source code id Software released in 1997. It plays Hexen with an OpenGL or Vulkan renderer at any frame rate, in widescreen and with mouselook, and its ZScript and ACS scripting run the largest library of mods any Doom engine has. Frontport installs it once per game, each with its own saves and settings, and Seeds your IWAD where UZDoom looks for it.

It takes Hexen 1.0 and 1.1, and the demo. The 2025 re-release waits until UZDoom recognizes its IWAD.

ports.name: Raze
ports.summary: Duke Nukem 3D on the GZDoom engine’s renderer, in widescreen at any frame rate.
ports.description:
Raze brings the Build engine games, Duke Nukem 3D among them, to the GZDoom engine, from the source code 3D Realms released in 2003. It plays Duke with an OpenGL or Vulkan renderer at any frame rate, in widescreen and with mouselook, and keeps the original’s look with its palette emulation. Frontport builds it from source, and Seeds your GRP where Raze looks for games.

It takes the free shareware episode, version 1.3D: DUKE3D.GRP from 3dduke13.zip, which 3D Realms let anyone share.

ports.name: Dethrace
ports.summary: Carmageddon rebuilt in C, function by function, from the original Windows 95 game.
ports.description:
Dethrace is a rebuild of Carmageddon, reverse-engineered from the original Windows 95 executable one function at a time and running natively on modern systems. Frontport builds it from source with SDL inside the app, because upstream’s Mac app expects SDL installed separately.

The game comes as a folder of files, or its zip. Frontport keeps a copy in the Port’s Data, where dethrace also keeps its options, key maps and saves, and settings such as Windowed = 1 go in dethrace.ini beside them. It accepts GOG’s Max Pack, which brings the CD music too, and the freeware demo from April 1997; the earlier demo from February doesn’t run. From GOG, add the installer you downloaded, setup_carmageddon_max_pack_1.0_gog_(77629).exe: Frontport unpacks it, and adds both Carmageddon and the Splat Pack. The first time, that builds the unpacker from source, which takes a few minutes.

ports.name: Dethrace
ports.summary: The Splat Pack, Carmageddon’s expansion, rebuilt in C from the original game’s code.
ports.description:
Dethrace rebuilds Carmageddon from the original Windows 95 executable, reverse-engineered one function at a time, and plays the Splat Pack expansion too: its 20 new races, new cars and new environments. Frontport builds it from source with SDL inside the app, because upstream’s Mac app expects SDL installed separately.

The Splat Pack comes as a folder of files. Frontport keeps a copy in the Port’s Data, where dethrace also keeps its options, key maps and saves, and settings such as Windowed = 1 go in dethrace.ini beside them. It accepts GOG’s Max Pack: add the installer you downloaded, setup_carmageddon_max_pack_1.0_gog_(77629).exe, and Frontport unpacks it and adds both the Splat Pack and Carmageddon. The first time, that builds the unpacker from source, which takes a few minutes.

ports.name: Arcanum Community Edition
ports.summary: Arcanum’s engine, re-implemented from its reverse-engineered code, for modern systems.
ports.description:
Arcanum Community Edition re-implements the engine of Arcanum from its reverse-engineered code, by the author of Fallout Community Edition, with the original gameplay. Upstream calls it a beta: the game is complete, but not everything has been tested. Frontport builds it from source with SDL inside the app, and makes it play from the Port’s Data instead of the folder the app sits in.

The game comes as Steam’s Arcanum, which Frontport finds in your Steam library once Steam has installed it. Frontport keeps a copy of the game’s files in the Port’s Data, where Arcanum also writes arcanum.cfg, its saves and the movies it unpacks.

ports.name: dhewm3
ports.summary: Doom 3 on its own source code, carried on for current systems, native on Apple silicon.
ports.description:
dhewm3 carries on the source code of Doom 3 that id Software released in 2011, with SDL and OpenAL in place of its Windows-only parts, widescreen, fixes for 64-bit systems and the original renderer and gameplay. Frontport builds it from source, natively for Apple silicon, with the game code of Doom 3 and Resurrection of Evil inside the app.

The game comes as Steam’s Doom 3, which Frontport finds in your Steam library once Steam has installed it. Frontport keeps a copy of its base folder in the Port’s Data, where dhewm3 also writes dhewm.cfg, its saves and its log.

ports.name: dhewm3
ports.summary: Resurrection of Evil on Doom 3’s own source code, carried on for current systems, native on Apple silicon.
ports.description:
dhewm3 carries on the source code of Doom 3 that id Software released in 2011, with SDL and OpenAL in place of its Windows-only parts, widescreen, fixes for 64-bit systems and the original renderer and gameplay. Frontport builds it from source, natively for Apple silicon, with the game code of Doom 3 and Resurrection of Evil inside the app.

The game comes as Steam’s Doom 3 and Resurrection of Evil, which Frontport finds in your Steam library once Steam has installed them. Frontport keeps a copy of their base and d3xp folders in the Port’s Data, where dhewm3 also writes dhewm.cfg, its saves and its log.

ports.name: RBDOOM-3-BFG
ports.summary: Doom 3: BFG Edition on its own source code, with a modern Vulkan renderer, native on Apple silicon.
ports.description:
RBDOOM-3-BFG carries on the source code of Doom 3: BFG Edition that id Software released in 2012, with a modern renderer: physically based lighting, HDR, shadow mapping, ambient occlusion and anti-aliasing, drawn with Vulkan, which MoltenVK turns into Metal. Frontport builds it from source, natively for Apple silicon, with MoltenVK and its shaders inside the app. It plays Doom 3, Resurrection of Evil and The Lost Mission, and the classic Doom and Doom II that come with the BFG Edition.

The game comes as Steam’s Doom 3: BFG Edition, which Frontport finds in your Steam library once Steam has installed it. Frontport keeps a copy of its base folder in the Port’s Data, where RBDOOM-3-BFG also writes D3BFGConfig.cfg and its saves. The baked lighting upstream ships separately isn’t included, so maps use the engine’s fallback lighting.

ports.name: Fallout Community Edition
ports.summary: Fallout’s engine, re-implemented from its reverse-engineered code, with bug fixes and higher resolutions.
ports.description:
Fallout Community Edition re-implements the engine of Fallout from its reverse-engineered code, with the original gameplay, fixes for the engine’s bugs and some quality-of-life improvements. Frontport builds it from source with SDL inside the app, and makes it play from the Port’s Data instead of the folder the app sits in.

The game comes as the folder of an installed copy or of its CD, or the CD’s image (.iso), which Frontport unpacks. Frontport keeps a copy of the game’s files in the Port’s Data, where Fallout also writes fallout.cfg and its saves, and the window’s size and full screen are set in f1_res.ini beside them. So far it accepts Steam’s Fallout, which Frontport finds in your Steam library once Steam has installed it, and the Russian CD published by 1C in 2008.

ports.name: Fallout 2 Community Edition
ports.summary: Fallout 2’s engine, re-implemented from its reverse-engineered code, with bug fixes, higher resolutions and sfall’s improvements.
ports.description:
Fallout 2 Community Edition re-implements the engine of Fallout 2 from its reverse-engineered code, with the original gameplay, fixes for the engine’s bugs, quality-of-life improvements and many of sfall’s features. Frontport builds it from source with SDL inside the app, and makes it play from the Port’s Data instead of the folder the app sits in.

The game comes as the folder of an installed copy. Frontport keeps a copy of the game’s files in the Port’s Data, where Fallout 2 also writes fallout2.cfg and its saves, and the window’s size and full screen are set in f2_res.ini beside them. So far it accepts Steam’s Fallout 2, which Frontport finds in your Steam library once Steam has installed it.

ports.name: OpenGothic
ports.summary: Gothic II and Night of the Raven on a new engine, with modern graphics, widescreen and high frame rates.
ports.description:
OpenGothic is a new engine for Gothic II and its add-on Night of the Raven, written from scratch and playing the original game’s data and scripts, with Metal graphics, widescreen resolutions and high frame rates. It plays with mouse and keyboard. Frontport builds it from source and wraps it in an app, because upstream’s Mac Release is a bare executable.

The game comes as the folder of an installed copy. Frontport keeps a copy of it in the Port’s Data, where OpenGothic also writes Gothic.ini, its saves and its log. So far it accepts Steam’s Gothic II: Gold Classic: add its folder, which Steam keeps in ~/Library/Application Support/Steam/steamapps/common/Gothic II once you install the game there, before it has been played.

ports.name: Xash3D FWGS
ports.summary: Half-Life on Xash3D FWGS, a GoldSrc-compatible engine, native on Apple silicon.
ports.description:
Xash3D FWGS is an engine compatible with GoldSrc, the engine of Half-Life, written without its code and carried on by the FWGS team; it plays the game with the game code Valve released in the Half-Life SDK, ported by FWGS to every platform the engine runs on. Frontport builds the engine and the game code from source, natively for Apple silicon.

Frontport keeps a copy of each game folder in the Port’s Data, where the engine also writes your settings and saves. Add the folder itself from Steam’s Half-Life folder (in Steam, Manage › Browse local files): valve. Frontport accepts the folder Steam for macOS installs. A folder you have played from has your saves and settings in it and won’t match the one Steam installs; Frontport can still keep it as that folder, Unverified.

ports.name: Xash3D FWGS
ports.summary: Opposing Force on Xash3D FWGS, a GoldSrc-compatible engine, native on Apple silicon.
ports.description:
Xash3D FWGS is an engine compatible with GoldSrc, the engine of Half-Life, written without its code and carried on by the FWGS team; it plays the game with the game code Valve released in the Half-Life SDK, ported by FWGS to every platform the engine runs on. Frontport builds the engine and the game code from source, natively for Apple silicon. This Port builds the game code of Opposing Force, from FWGS’s port of it.

Frontport keeps a copy of each game folder in the Port’s Data, where the engine also writes your settings and saves. Add the folder itself from Steam’s Half-Life folder (in Steam, Manage › Browse local files): gearbox, and valve, the Half-Life folder Opposing Force builds on. Frontport accepts the folders Steam installs. A folder you have played from has your saves and settings in it and won’t match the one Steam installs; Frontport can still keep it as that folder, Unverified.

ports.name: Xash3D FWGS
ports.summary: Blue Shift on Xash3D FWGS, a GoldSrc-compatible engine, native on Apple silicon.
ports.description:
Xash3D FWGS is an engine compatible with GoldSrc, the engine of Half-Life, written without its code and carried on by the FWGS team; it plays the game with the game code Valve released in the Half-Life SDK, ported by FWGS to every platform the engine runs on. Frontport builds the engine and the game code from source, natively for Apple silicon. This Port builds the game code of Blue Shift, from FWGS’s port of it.

Frontport keeps a copy of each game folder in the Port’s Data, where the engine also writes your settings and saves. Add the folder itself from Steam’s Half-Life folder (in Steam, Manage › Browse local files): bshift, and valve, the Half-Life folder Blue Shift builds on. Frontport accepts the folders Steam installs. A folder you have played from has your saves and settings in it and won’t match the one Steam installs; Frontport can still keep it as that folder, Unverified.

ports.name: OpenSupaplex
ports.summary: Supaplex, reimplemented in C from its disassembled code, with the original levels included.
ports.description:
OpenSupaplex is a one-to-one reimplementation of Supaplex in C, written from the disassembled code of the DOS game with its speed fix and checked against thousands of recorded demos, so it plays exactly as the original. It adds music and sound effects, save states, scaling modes and game controller support. Frontport builds it from source, with SDL inside the app. The original game is freeware and its files come with the app, the 111 levels and the extra level sets included, so it needs no ROM.

OpenSupaplex keeps its settings, players, Hall of Fame and saved games in the Port’s Data.

ports.name: Cannonball
ports.summary: OutRun’s arcade code, ported to C++, with widescreen, 60 fps and time trials.
ports.description:
Cannonball is an enhanced OutRun engine: the arcade game’s 68000 code, ported routine by routine to C++ and running natively. It adds widescreen, 60 fps, a high-resolution mode, time trials, continuous mode and game controller support, and keeps the original’s music, attract mode and high score tables. Frontport builds it from source with SDL inside the app, because upstream publishes Windows builds only.

It plays from the arcade’s ROMs: revision B, MAME’s outrun set, as its folder or zip. Frontport keeps a copy in the Port’s Data, where Cannonball also keeps its high scores and config.xml, whose settings its menu changes.

ports.name: OpenLara
ports.summary: Tomb Raider on a new engine, with widescreen, smooth frame rates and modern controls.
ports.description:
OpenLara is a new engine for the classic Tomb Raider games, written from scratch and playing the original levels, with widescreen, frame rates beyond the original’s 30 fps, a free camera, and keyboard and game controller support. Frontport builds it from source and makes it play from the Port’s Data instead of the folder the app sits in, and reads game controllers through macOS, so any it supports works.

The game comes as Steam’s Tomb Raider I-III Remastered, which holds the original Tomb Raider in its folder 1: Frontport finds it in your Steam library once Steam has installed it, or downloads it with Steam. Frontport keeps a copy of that folder in the Port’s Data, where OpenLara also keeps its settings and saves, and plays its music and the PlayStation videos from it.

ports.name: The Ur-Quan Masters
ports.summary: Star Control II, from the source code of its 3DO version, with its voices and soundtrack.
ports.description:
The Ur-Quan Masters is the open-source port of Star Control II, built from the source code Toys for Bob released in 2002 for the game’s 3DO version. It plays the whole adventure across the galaxy and its ship-to-ship battles, and Super Melee for two players on one Mac, scaled up to a larger window or full screen with smoothing filters, with keyboard and game controller support. Frontport builds it from source, with SDL inside the app. The game’s content is freeware and comes with the app, with the 3DO version’s full voice acting and soundtrack, so it needs no ROM.

The Ur-Quan Masters keeps its settings, saved games and Super Melee teams in the Port’s Data.

ports.name: OpenTTD
ports.summary: Transport Tycoon Deluxe, remade and expanded, with free graphics, sounds and music included.
ports.description:
OpenTTD is the open-source remake of Transport Tycoon Deluxe, begun from the reverse-engineered original and developed for over twenty years. Build road, rail, sea and air networks, carry passengers and cargo between growing towns and industries, and compete with AI companies or play online with others. It adds much larger maps, signals and timetables, a scenario editor, and thousands of free vehicle sets, maps and scripts from its online content service. Frontport builds it from source. OpenGFX, OpenSFX and OpenMSX, free replacements for the original game’s graphics, sounds and music, come with the app, so it needs no ROM.

OpenTTD keeps its settings, saved games, screenshots and downloaded content in the Port’s Data.

ports.name: b3x
ports.summary: Burnout 3: Takedown, statically recompiled from your Xbox disc, with Vulkan graphics.
ports.description:
b3x is a static recompilation of the Xbox version of Burnout 3: Takedown: the toolkit xboxrecomp lifts every function of the game’s executable, instruction by instruction, to C, which then runs natively on Apple silicon, with the Xbox’s graphics chip drawn through Vulkan and its audio processor mixed in software. Every mode plays, from races and Road Rage to Crash, with split-screen for two players and a game controller. Frontport builds it from source and makes the game’s code from your disc during the build, so none of it is ever downloaded; the first build takes a long while.

b3x keeps its saves and the Xbox’s hard disk in the Port’s Data.

ports.name: vkQuake
ports.summary: Quake on Vulkan, fast and smooth at any frame rate, native on Apple silicon.
ports.description:
vkQuake carries on QuakeSpasm, the Quake engine built up from the source code id Software released in 1999, with a Vulkan renderer that MoltenVK turns into Metal. It renders on several threads, runs at any frame rate without breaking the game’s physics, draws the underwater warp as the software renderer did, and plays the mods QuakeSpasm plays, such as Arcane Dimensions. Frontport builds it from source, natively for Apple silicon, with MoltenVK inside the app.

The game comes as the id1 folder of Quake: the shareware episode, from the shareware release’s install. Frontport keeps a copy of it in the Port’s Data, where vkQuake also writes vkQuake.cfg and its saves.

ports.name: Yamagi Quake II
ports.summary: Quake II as it shipped, fixed and sharpened, native on Apple silicon.
ports.description:
Yamagi Quake II is the Quake II engine built up from the source code id Software released in 2001, kept true to the original game while fixing its bugs. It renders with OpenGL 3.2, OpenGL 1.4 or the original software renderer, runs at any frame rate and resolution without changing the game’s physics, and plays sound through OpenAL with the underwater effects. Frontport builds it from source, natively for Apple silicon.

The game comes as the baseq2 folder of Quake II: the original game’s, from Steam’s Quake II, or the demo’s, with its first levels. Frontport keeps a copy of it in the Port’s Data, where Yamagi Quake II also writes config.cfg, its saves and screenshots.

ports.name: VCMI
ports.summary: Heroes of Might and Magic III on a new open-source engine, with mods, online play and a map editor.
ports.description:
VCMI is an open-source engine for Heroes of Might and Magic III, written anew to play the original game’s files. It runs the Shadow of Death campaigns and maps at any resolution, with smoother animations, an improved interface and AI, and online multiplayer through its lobby. Its launcher installs mods from VCMI’s repository, among them Horn of the Abyss and Wake of Gods, and opens its map editor.

The game comes as the Data, Maps and Mp3 folders of Heroes III Complete or Shadow of Death, together in one folder. Frontport keeps a copy of them in the Port’s Data, where VCMI also keeps its settings, mods and saves.

ports.name: PvZ-Portable
ports.summary: Plants vs. Zombies: Game of the Year Edition, reimplemented to play natively on Apple silicon.
ports.description:
PvZ-Portable is a community reimplementation of Plants vs. Zombies: Game of the Year Edition, written from public research and play-testing to recreate the original almost exactly: Adventure, the mini-games, puzzles, Survival and the Zen Garden. It renders through OpenGL and SDL, and reads the original game’s profiles and saves. Frontport builds it from source, natively for Apple silicon, and applies the text fixes upstream’s script makes for Steam’s edition as the game starts.

The game comes as the original’s main.pak and properties folder: Steam’s Mac edition installs them inside its app, and its Windows edition in its folder; Frontport finds either in your Steam library, or downloads it with Steam. Frontport keeps a copy of them in the Port’s Data, where PvZ-Portable also keeps its settings and saves.

ports.name: ScummVM
ports.summary: The Secret of Monkey Island on ScummVM’s reimplementation of LucasArts’ SCUMM engine.
ports.description:
ScummVM reimplements the engines of classic adventure games, so they play natively from their original files. Its SCUMM engine plays LucasArts’ adventures, among them The Secret of Monkey Island as the Special Edition carries it: the classic 1990 game inside it. ScummVM can’t yet decode the Special Edition’s music, which is in Microsoft’s xWMA format, so the game plays without music. Frontport builds ScummVM from source with its SCUMM engine.

The game comes as Steam’s The Secret of Monkey Island: Special Edition: Frontport finds it in your Steam library once Steam has installed it, or downloads it with Steam. Frontport keeps a copy of it in the Port’s Data, and ScummVM starts the game from there; it keeps its settings and saves in the Port’s Data too.
